<meta>This page is the formal title page of the work, following the flyleaf that contained modern archival markings. It identifies this volume as a collection of astrological rules and principles compiled from several of the most influential authorities in the history of the practice.</meta>

# ASTROLOGY
## IN APHORISMS <term>aphorisms: concise statements of principles, rules, or observations, designed here as a quick-reference guide for practicing astrologers</term>

-> THE WORKS OF PTOLEMY, HERMES, <-
<note>Ptolemy (c. 100–170 AD) was the author of the Tetrabiblos, the foundational text of Western astrology; Hermes refers to Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary Hellenistic figure to whom many foundational esoteric texts were attributed.</note>
-> LOUIS DE RIGIIS, <-
<note>Louis de Rigiis (Ludovicus de Rigiis) was a 15th-century astrologer known for his work on aphorisms and the "Aphorismi Astrologici."</note>
-> ALMANSOR, GEROLAMO <-
<note>Almansor likely refers to Yahya ibn Abi Mansur (died c. 830), a prominent astronomer in the court of the Abbasid Caliph Al-Ma'mun. Gerolamo Cardano (1501–1576) was a famous Italian polymath, physician, and astrologer.</note>

--- Page 4 ---
<meta>This page continues the front matter of the 1641 Ulm edition of Aphoristic Astrology. It serves as an introduction "To the Reader," explaining the editorial logic behind organizing various astrological maxims—originally disorganized—into a systematic structure based on Ptolemy’s classic work.</meta>

¶ 2

## To the Reader.

It has always been the custom of those who have handed down Aphoristic Doctrine <note>This refers to teaching through "aphorisms"—short, pithy statements of truth or principle rather than long essays.</note> to set out sentences that are scattered here and there and not connected to one another. In this same way, the authors of this small book, wishing to present their astrology in an aphoristic style, observe no specific order in the statements they provide. However, because a proper arrangement and systematic order of teaching is required to make astrological judgments—whether for a birth chart <term>genitura; a chart cast for the moment of birth</term>, a solar return <term>revolutio; a chart cast for the anniversary of a birth to predict the year ahead</term>, or a decumbiture <term>decubitus; a chart cast for the moment a person first takes to their bed with illness</term> (as well as other astrological figures)—it was necessary to organize these scattered sentences and aphorisms back into their proper chapters. The subjects treated by these authors primarily concern human Nativities (births); and therefore, since this treatise is of such high quality, the aphorisms relating to births have been organized into chapters following the order used in Ptolemy's <note>Claudius Ptolemy was a 2nd-century scholar whose work formed the foundation of Western astrology.</note> *Tetrabiblos* <note>original: "Quadrip[artitum]"; literally the "Four-Part Book," the standard textbook of astrology in the 17th century.</note>. Furthermore, because the analysis of solar returns (revolutions) contributes greatly to the understanding of a birth chart, the aphorisms regarding these yearly charts have also been arranged in their own section. Additionally, since the study of decumbiture charts is essential for understanding matters of life and death...

<column-break/>

...knowledge, a series of aphorisms concerning these medical charts has been compiled in this book. However, because many aphorisms might have been overlooked if they did not fit into a specific chapter—specifically those that could not be reduced to any of the categories mentioned above—they have been collected under the title of "Notable Aphorisms." Through your knowledge of Ptolemy and a careful study of these aphorisms, you, diligent reader, will be well-equipped to judge birth charts with the greatest skill.

<summary>This preface explains that the book organizes previously scattered astrological maxims into a systematic order based on Ptolemy’s Tetrabiblos to make them more practical for doctors and astrologers. It categorizes the content into birth charts, yearly returns, medical astrology, and general notable observations.</summary>
<keywords>astrology, aphorisms, Ptolemy, birth charts, solar returns, decumbiture, medical astrology, Tetrabiblos</keywords>

### APHORISMS.

->Those which could not be reduced to the Chapters pertaining to nativities, to revolutions, and to the Falling Ill [decumbiture], are placed here under the title of Notable Aphorisms, as they are worthy of observation and should be read through by the Reader.<-
<note>nativitates: birth charts; revolutiones: solar returns or annual charts used to predict events for the coming year.</note>

# CLAUDIUS PTOLEMY'S
## One Hundred SAYINGS, or
### The Fruit of His
### Books.

<note>This text, known as the Centiloquium, is a collection of 100 astrological aphorisms. Although traditionally attributed to Claudius Ptolemy, modern scholars believe it was likely written by a later Arabic or Greek author and attributed to him to give it authority.</note>

1. **F**rom you, and from science <note>original: "A Te, & à scientia"</note>. For it cannot be that one who is knowledgeable can predict the specific forms of things, just as the senses do not perceive a specific form of a sensible thing, but rather a certain general form; and it is necessary for the one treating these matters to use conjecture, for only those inspired by the divine predict specifics.

2. When the person who consults [the astrologer] examines himself better, there will be no difference between himself and the form of his question.

3. He who is suited for a certain matter will surely have a very powerful star of this kind of significance in his birth chart <note>original: "genitura," referring to the horoscope at the moment of birth</note>.

4. A soul naturally suited for the knowledge of truth achieves more than one who has trained himself to the highest degree in the science.

5. One who is knowledgeable can avert many effects of the stars, when he knows their nature, and [prepares] himself <note>The text suggests that astrological influence is not absolute fate, but can be mitigated by wisdom and preparation.</note>

<sig>A</sig>
<meta>catchword: before</meta>

<summary>This page contains the final section of an index of astrological aphorisms followed by the opening of the "Centiloquium," a famous set of 100 astrological rules attributed to Ptolemy. The first few aphorisms discuss the limits of astrological knowledge and the importance of the practitioner's natural intuition.</summary>

<keywords>Claudius Ptolemy, Centiloquium, astrology, aphorisms, birth charts, prediction, conjecture, scientific knowledge, divination</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the "Centiloquium" (One Hundred Sayings) attributed to Claudius Ptolemy, picking up from the end of Aphorism 5. The text focuses on the practical application of astrology in daily life, medicine, and politics, emphasizing that a wise person can use the stars as a guide rather than being a slave to fate.</meta>

...to prepare before their arrival. <note>This concludes Aphorism 5, which discusses how a knowledgeable person can mitigate the stars' influence.</note>

6. The selection of days and hours is only useful when the time has been well established by the birth chart <note>original: genitura</note>. For if the birth chart is unfavorable, the selection will be of no use, even if it seems to look toward a good outcome.

7. No one can perceive the mixtures of the Stars unless they have first learned their natural differences and combinations.

8. A wise soul assists the celestial operation, just as the best farmer assists nature by plowing and weeding.

9. In the process of birth and decay, physical forms are affected by celestial forms. Therefore, those who make talismans <note>original: imagines; literally "images," referring to astrological amulets</note> use these influences, observing when the stars have entered into them.

10. In choosing days and hours, use the malefic planets <note>Mars and Saturn</note> just as a great Physician uses poisons moderately for a cure.

11. Do not choose a day or an hour before you have learned the quality of the matter proposed.

12. Love and hatred prevent true judgments from being reached, for they diminish the greatest things and enlarge the smallest.

13. When the celestial configuration signifies something, use both the helping and

<column-break/>

<page-num>3</page-num>
<sig>A 2</sig>
<meta>The catchword "cor-" connects the word "corruptiuis" from the bottom of column 1 to the top of column 2.</meta>

the corrupting Stars—that is, the secondary ones. <note>In this context, secondary stars are those that modify the main influence of the primary planets.</note>

14. To what great errors is the Astrologer subject when the seventh house <note>locus septimus</note> and its Lord are afflicted. <note>In traditional astrology, the 7th house represents the "other" or the public; if this house is poorly positioned, the astrologer's judgment is often clouded.</note>

15. The rising signs of the enemies of a kingdom are the signs declining <note>cadent</note> from the rising sign of the kingdom itself. However, the rising signs of friends are the angles <note>cardines</note> and the succeeding houses. The same rule applies to systems of belief.

16. When benefic planets are in the eighth house, they bring loss from good men; but if the planets are well-disposed, they will avert that loss.

17. When you judge the life of any old man, do not give a verdict until you have measured how many years he is physically capable of living.

18. When both Luminaries <note>The Sun and the Moon</note> are at the same degree, if a benefic planet is rising, the newborn will be fortunate in everything that happens to them; likewise if they are opposite each other at sunrise and sunset. But if a malefic planet is in the ascendant, you should judge the opposite.

19. The power of a purgation <note>a medical treatment to cleanse the body</note> is weakened when the Moon is joined to Jupiter.

20. Do not strike a limb with iron <note>perform surgery</note> when the Moon holds the zodiac sign that rules that specific limb. <note>A fundamental rule of medieval medicine: for example, one should not operate on the head when the Moon is in Aries.</note>

21. When the Sun <note>original: astrological symbol for the Sun</note> is in Aries <note>original: astrological symbol for Aries</note> or Leo <note>original: astrological symbol for Leo</note>...

<summary>This page lists several astrological aphorisms (6-20) from the Centiloquium, covering the importance of the birth chart, the comparison between astrology and medicine/farming, and specific rules for medical surgery and political alliances based on the stars.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the "Centiloquium," a collection of 100 astrological aphorisms traditionally attributed to Ptolemy. This section (aphorisms 21-33) covers medical astrology, electional astrology (choosing the right time for actions like making clothes), and mundane astrology (the fate of kings and kingdoms).</meta>

21. If the Lord of the ascendant <note>the planet ruling the sign rising on the eastern horizon</note> is joined to a Star placed under the earth, it is a good time to use purgatives <note>medicines to induce bowel movements</note>. If, however, it is joined to a Star positioned above the earth, whoever takes the potion will instead vomit.

22. You should neither put on a new garment for the first time nor cut the fabric when the Sun [☉] is located in the Dragon's Tail <note>original: ☋; the South Node of the Moon, traditionally considered a point of depletion or bad luck</note>. It is even worse if the Sun is otherwise poorly afflicted <note>in a weak or difficult astrological position</note> at that time.

23. The configuration of the Moon to the Stars makes the native <note>the person for whom the chart is cast</note> quite agile. If those stars are powerful, they indicate an effective impulse to act; but if they are weak, they indicate a sluggishness in action.

24. An eclipse of the Luminaries <note>the Sun and Moon</note> occurring in the angles <note>original: cardinibus; the four most powerful points of a chart</note> of a birth chart or of annual revolutions is harmful. The timing of the effect is taken from the distance between the ascendant and the place of the eclipse. Just as you count years from the hours of a Solar Eclipse, you count months from the hours of a Lunar Eclipse.

25. Calculate the progression of the Ruler <note>the planet in charge of a specific life area</note> by the ascensions of the sphere when it is positioned in the Midheaven <note>original: medio Cæli; the highest point in the sky</note>; however, when it is located in the ascendant, do so by the ascensions of the climate <note>the specific latitude of the location</note>.

26. A matter remains entirely hidden when the Star signifying it is joined to the Sun either under the earth or in a foreign place <note>a sign where the planet has no traditional dignity or strength</note>; conversely, the matter is revealed when the star is raised from a low point to a height <column-break/>

<meta>catchword: tol- (connecting "tollitur")</meta>

<page-num>5</page-num>

and is placed in its own proper place.

27. Venus brings pleasure to that part of the body ruled by the sign in which she is located. The same principle applies to the other Stars <note>planets</note>.

28. When you are unable to join the Moon to two [benefic] Stars, manage at least to join her to a Fixed Star that possesses the combined nature of those two.

29. The Fixed Stars bring about irrational and marvelous successes, yet they often mark these with great calamities unless the Planets also agree with the success.

30. Examine the inaugurations <note>original: creationes; the moment a king's reign begins</note> of the first Kings of a lineage. For if the ascendant of that inauguration agrees with the ascendant of the birth chart of the King's son, that son will be the successor to the Kingdom.

31. When the ruler of a Kingdom falls into a climacteric place <note>original: locum climactericum; a critical or dangerous degree, often associated with ages 7, 9, or their multiples</note>, then either the King or someone great among the Princes of the Kingdom will die.

32. A suitable configuration of Stars—representing the nature of the matter from which goodwill is established in the birth charts of both—creates concord between two people.

33. Love and hatred arise both from the concord and discord of the luminaries <note>the Sun and Moon</note> and from the ascendants of the birth charts of both parties...

is discovered. Moreover, signs of obedience increase goodwill.

34. If the ruler or the "host" planet of the New Moon <note>original: interlunij; the period of the lunar cycle when the moon is invisible</note> is found in an angle <note>original: cardinalis; the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses of a chart, which are the most powerful</note>, it signifies whatever events are to come in that month.

35. When the Sun [☉] reaches the position of any Star, it excites the power that the star holds over the air <note>referring to weather patterns and atmospheric changes</note>.

36. In the founding of Cities, use the Fixed Stars <note>stars that do not move relative to one another, unlike planets</note> that are favorable. In the building of houses, however, use the wandering stars <note>the planets</note>. Kings of any City that have Mars [♂] at its highest point <note>original: culminantem; at the Midheaven or 10th house</note> usually perish by the sword.

37. Those who have Scorpio [♏] or Pisces [♓] as their ascendant <note>original: horoscopum; the sign rising on the eastern horizon</note> will be the cause of their own power. Those whose ascendant is Aries [♈] or Libra [♎] will be the cause of their own death. You shall reason in the same way regarding the other signs.

38. When Mercury [☿], positioned in one of the houses of Saturn [♄] <note>Capricorn or Aquarius</note>, is powerful, it gives the person born a contemplative intellect and a talent for investigating things. But in a house of Mars [♂] <note>Aries or Scorpio</note>, and especially in Aries [♈], it gives eloquence.

39. The affliction <note>harmful influence from a difficult planet</note> of the eleventh house during the coronation of a King signifies loss for both his household and his finances. However, the affliction of the second house signifies the loss of the money in his treasury <note>original: ouilis; literally "sheepfold," often used metaphorically for wealth or property</note>.

40. When the ascendant is oppressed by malefic planets <note>traditionally Saturn or Mars</note>, the person born at that time will delight in filthy things and will appreciate foul-smelling odors.

41. Beware the affliction of the eighth house and its ruler at the time of departure, but beware the affliction of the second house and its ruler at the time of return.

42. A disease that begins when the Sun [☉] is in the sign that a malefic planet held in the birth chart <note>original: genitura</note>, or in a square [□] or opposition [☍] to it, will be extremely grave. If a malefic planet looks upon it <note>aspects it</note>, it is dangerous; if it is in a place where a benefic planet <note>traditionally Jupiter or Venus</note> was at the time of birth, it will be without danger.

43. Contrary configurations of the times <note>current planetary movements</note> intensify the harmful figures of a person's race <note>original: gentis; likely referring to inherited traits or national characteristics</note>.

44. It is harmful when the ascendant of a sick person is at odds with the figures of their own birth chart, and the time has not reached a benefic planet.

45. Anyone who does not have the rulers of their birth chart or the ascendant in human signs <note>signs depicted as humans: Gemini, Virgo, Libra, and the front half of Sagittarius or Aquarius</note> will be a stranger to humanity, even to themselves.

46. Great fortunes are granted in birth charts by the Fixed Stars, by the angles of the New Moons, and by the placement of the "Lot of Fortune" <note>original: partis fortunae; a mathematical point in a chart representing prosperity</note> of the Kingdom, when the ascendant is found among them.

47. In a birth chart <note>original: genitura; a calculation of the positions of the stars at the moment of birth</note>, when a malefic planet <note>original: malefica; planets considered naturally difficult, specifically Saturn or Mars</note> falls into the same position where a benefic planet <note>original: beneficæ; planets considered naturally helpful, specifically Jupiter or Venus</note> is located in another person’s chart, the one who has the benefic planet will be harmed by the one who has the malefic.

48. When the highest point <note>original: culmen; the Midheaven or 10th house, representing authority and career</note> of the Master (that is, the Ruler) is the Ascendant <note>original: horoscopus; the sign rising on the eastern horizon</note> of the subject, or if their rulers are arranged in a favorable configuration, they will remain inseparable for a long time. The same is true when the sixth house <note>the house of service and health</note> of a servant is found to be the Ascendant of the Master.

49. When the Ascendant of a subject is the highest point in the Master's birth chart, the Master will have such great faith in that subject that the Master will be commanded by him.

50. Do not overlook the 119 conjunctions <note>this refers to a traditional calculation of the various ways the seven classical planets can pair or group together</note>; for in these is placed the knowledge of those things which happen in the world, and of generation and corruption.

51. Take the sign in which the Sun [☉] is located at the time of birth and make that the Ascendant at the time of conception; and whatever sign was found to be the Ascendant at conception (or its opposite), make that the Ascendant at birth. <note>This refers to the "Trutine of Hermes," a traditional method used to calculate the exact moment of conception based on the birth chart.</note>

52. The rulers of the birth charts of men of tall stature are in "sublimities" <note>original: sublimitatibus; high-altitude or high-honor positions in the sky</note>, and their Ascendants are at the beginning of the signs. However, the rulers of those who are of short stature are found in "humilities" <note>original: humilitatibus; low-altitude or weakened positions</note>. In addition to this, examine whether the signs are

---

<page-num>9</page-num>

straight or oblique. <note>original: recta, an obliqua; "straight" signs take longer to rise over the horizon, while "oblique" signs rise more quickly, affecting the physical appearance.</note>

53. The rulers of the birth charts of thin men have no latitude <note>original: latitudinem; the distance of a planet north or south of the ecliptic, or the sun's path</note>, while those of fat men do. If the latitude is southern, they will be agile; if northern, they will be sluggish.

54. Rulers in buildings <note>referring to planetary rulers of a construction project</note> where "underground" stars <note>planets located below the horizon or in the 4th house</note> are joined together, hinder the raising of the building.

55. The harmful power of Mars [♂] against ships is diminished when it is neither in the middle of the sky <note>the Midheaven</note> nor in the 11th house. For in these places it destroys the ship, with pirates seizing it by force. The ship will be burned, however, if the Ascendant is afflicted by any fixed star that is of a mixed nature with Mars [♂].

56. When the Sun [☉] is in the first quadrant—that is, from the point it moves away from its conjunction with the Moon—the moisture of bodies flows out until the second quadrant; in the remaining quadrants, however, it decreases.

57. When you see the seventh house <note>the house of the "other," here representing the physician</note> and its ruler afflicted during an illness, change the doctor.

58. Look at the place of the conjunction <note>the meeting of the Sun and Moon</note> and where it sits in relation to the Ascendant of the year; if the profection <note>term: profection; a system where the chart is "rotated" by one sign for every year of life</note> reaches that place, then the event will occur.

59. Regarding an absent person, do not pronounce what has happened to them before you see the...

<page-num>10</page-num>

...became drunk, nor that he received a wound, before you have inquired whether he has had blood let <note>original: sanguis ei missus fuerit; bloodletting was a common medical practice, and its astrological signatures could mimic those of a violent injury</note>, nor that he found treasures, before you have searched whether he perhaps received a deposit <note>i.e., someone else's money left for safekeeping</note>, since the appearances of all these things are similar.

60. Regarding the sick, inspect the critical days and the Sun’s [☉] passage through the angles of a sixteen-sided figure: for where you find those angles well-disposed, it will go well for the person suffering; conversely, it will go poorly if you find them afflicted.

61. The Sun [☉] signifies those things which pertain to the body, such as those things which are familiar to it for its movement.

62. When you calculate the exact minute of the beginning of a conjunction <note>original: coniunctionis; here referring to the New Moon</note>, you can judge the change of the weather for that month; for the judgment will be according to the ruler of the angle of each figure, for this ruler overcomes the nature of the air, taking also into account the quality of the current season.

63. When Saturn [♄] and Jupiter [♃] are conjoined, see which of them is more elevated <note>original: sublimior; the planet with the higher northern latitude or higher in the house structure</note>, and pronounce judgment according to his nature. Do the same for the other Stars <note>planets</note>.

64. # THE BOOK
### OF THE HUNDRED
## APHORISMS
#### OF HERMES.

1. The **Sun** [☉] and **Moon** [☽], after God, are the life of all living things. The births <note>original: *natiuitates*; refers to the birth chart or horoscope of an individual</note> of many indeed do not have a *hyleg* <term>hyleg: the "Giver of Life," a specific planet or point in a chart used to calculate a person's lifespan</term>, but because the **Sun** and **Moon** behold their Ascendant <note>the sign rising on the eastern horizon</note> with love, and the same being free <note>from affliction by "bad" planets</note>, their life is prolonged further.

2. All daytime births are strengthened by the **Sun** [☉], when it is well-configured with the benefics <note>the "good" planets, Jupiter and Venus</note>. Nighttime births, however, [are strengthened] by the **Moon** [☽], when she is beheld by the benefics; and if this is not the case, yet if there be good planets in the angles <note>the most powerful positions in a chart: the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses</note>, then the birth is fortunate.

3. **Mars** [♂], when he is the lord of the Ascendant in the tenth house <note>the house of career and public standing</note>, grants dignity and power to the person born, which they will use with injury and cruelty; and this is called a misfortune rather than good fortune.

4. **Jupiter** [♃], when configured with the malefics <note>the "harmful" planets, Saturn and Mars</note>, changes their malice into good. **Venus** [♀]...

5. The Astrologer cannot perform the blending of the stars' significations until he knows their friendships and enmities. 7. You should make the **Sun** [☉] or one of the superior planets <note>the "outer" planets: Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn</note> the significator of Great Princes. 8. An aspect <note>the angular relationship between planets</note> cannot diminish the signification of a conjunction [☌]. But a conjunction diminishes the signification of an aspect, for a conjunction is stronger than an aspect.

10. The sixth [6th] or twelfth [12th] places <note>the 6th and 12th houses, traditionally considered "bad" or "malefic" houses</note> are bad for the benefics <note>the "good" planets, Jupiter and Venus</note> when they are hindered there by the malefics <note>Saturn and Mars</note>.

11. Rumors reported while the **Sun** [☉] is in the first face <term>face: also known as a decan, a 10-degree division of a zodiac sign</term> of **Cancer** [♋︎] are lies and fabricated.

12. Sometimes judgments in the questions <note>original: *quaestionibus*; referring to Horary astrology, where a chart is cast to answer a specific question</note> of astrologers are not true, either because of an error in their instruments, or because of the ignorance of the person asking, or when the **Sun** [☉] is near the degree of the Midheaven <term>Midheaven: the highest point in the chart, also called Medium Coeli</term>, or when the configurations that grant or deny the matter are equal.

13. While the **Sun** [☉] is southern, descending in **Aquarius** [♒︎] or **Pisces** [♓︎], do not begin building; for a structure of this kind is quickly destroyed.

14. It is necessary for **Mercury** [☿] to be strong through harmonious places and through the configurations of other stars in birth charts, so that the person born may have dignity; for **Mercury** by itself is a weak planet.

15. In signs of two bodies <note>original: *duorum corporum*; refers to the "mutable" signs—Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, and Pisces—which were thought to have a dual nature</note>, victory is good and defeat is bad, for both outcomes are doubled.

44 It happens that even a skilled Astrologer may err when he is ignorant of the significator <note>the specific planet representing the person or topic</note> of the one for whom he makes a choice.

45 **Saturn** [♄] elevated above **Venus** [♀] by a square aspect [□] <note>a harsh 90-degree angle</note> makes children unchaste and women impatient. If, however, **Venus** [♀] is elevated above **Saturn** [♄], she will make men easy and prone toward women.

97 The meanings of the Stars are always varied whenever their **latitudes** <note>the distance of a planet north or south of the ecliptic line</note> vary in their configurations with one another.

98 The **Sun** [☉] in the fourth, seventh, ninth, or twelfth **house** <note>specific divisions of the astrological chart</note> indicates that the matter in question has already been asked about. The same is indicated if the Sun has separated from **Mercury** [☿]. If, however, the **ascendant** <note>the sign rising on the eastern horizon</note> is a **bicorporeal sign** <note>original: "signum bicorporeum"; also called "double-bodied" or mutable signs, like Gemini or Pisces</note> and the **Sun** [☉] is similarly in a bicorporeal sign, the same matter is being sought after a second time.

99 If a **malefic planet** <note>original: "malus"; typically Saturn or Mars</note> is in its own **house** or **exaltation** <note>signs where a planet is strongest</note>, it shows a good conclusion, though it may arrive with delay. If, however, that same planet is hindered in the **ascendant**, even if it is in its own house or exaltation, it nonetheless brings about hindrance and a bad end.

100 The final outcome of every undertaking and of all doubtful matters is determined by these **significators** <note>planets or points that represent the person or the question</note>: namely, by the **fourth house** and its lord, and by any planet that may be within it. Likewise, by the **Luminary** <note>the Sun or Moon</note> that holds authority, and its lord, and by the planet to which that Luminary is joined, and its lord.

Use these and the other things I have handed down to you clearly; by using them with sobriety, you will never err, with God’s help.

# ASTROLOGICAL
## APHORISMS
### OF LUDOVICO
### DE REGIIS

->To the Patriarch of<-
->Constantinople.<-

1 Judgments of future things are not granted except to those experienced in the condition of their planets at their specific times, according to their innate power. Indeed, those who pronounce judgments based on a single aphorism alone are in error.

2 The locations of the **fixed stars** and the **apogees** <note>original: "Augiumque"; the points where planets are furthest from the Earth</note> have changed and change daily; the face of the heavens never remains exactly as it was.

3 One must not be certain about the condition of any Planet unless you first certify yourself regarding the **dispositors** <note>the planets that rule the sign where another planet is currently located</note> of that place, checking for any ill-disposition, as well as their **exaltation** and **Lordship**.

4 A Planet demonstrates a small outcome if its **dispositors** <note>the planets that rule the signs where other planets are located</note> indicate otherwise regarding their essential state of good or evil.

5 **Mercury** [☿] in the houses of **Mars** [♂] <note>Aries or Scorpio</note> makes the person born fickle. If **Mars** [♂] is in **Aquarius** [♒] and the **Sun** [☉] is in **Aries** [♈], **Mercury** [☿] will not remain there if it was present; or if both are strong, and you have not judged them to be in a good state of fortune, we have said this regarding **Mercury** [☿]. For it is a more universal planet and does not tend toward the transformation of its own nature.

6 The **significators** <note>planets representing the person or question</note> or the lords of a place are removed from the judgment of the Planet, although it may demonstrate its nature in some part for a time.

7 The **Lord of the Hour** <note>the planet ruling the specific hour of the day</note> must be considered in all forms and figures, as well as the lord of the place of conjunction which is called **Anauba** <note>original: "Anauba"; a technical term for the participating ruler or a specific planetary power</note>; these are a kind of steering-oar for the matter being questioned, like one who is a more powerful and strong leader of the [astrological] figure.

8 Births that occur during the appearance of **Comets**, having the angle of that ascendant or the **Midheaven** <note>original: "medij Coeli"; the highest point in the sky at the time of birth</note> of the sign in which the Comet appeared—if the Lord of the House and the Lord of Exaltation of that strong angle are present—will indicate to the newborns that some other singular and most great event is coming, far beyond what is signified by their own personal figure; and if that sign falls, and the Comet has a motion that is

9 Kingdoms and dominions, faiths, sects, and the opinions of men are changed while the **auges** <note>original: "auges"; the apogee or point where a planet is furthest from the Earth</note> of the planets change from sign to sign—I speak of those nations whose significator is the planet of the changed apogee. And the change will be for good or evil according to the nature of those higher significators of those times, and according to the nature of the sign of the change.

If they stand strong in their births by mixing the given factors—the Lord of the House and the Lord of Exaltation together. If they are weak, however, even if they were good, the time designates that their laws and sayings will remain for only a short time.

# THE PROPOSITIONS OF ALMANSOR
## The Astrologer’s Propositions to the King of the Saracens.

> *My King, you requested a small compendium of aphorisms <note>original: "Aphorismorum compendiolum"</note>. In order to satisfy your wishes, I have by no means refused to undertake the labor. I have written them; I pray you receive them with a favorable mind.*

1 The arrangement of the signs, as I shall say, begins from **Aries** <note>original symbol: ♈</note>; specifically, one is diurnal <note>active during the day</note>, while the other is nocturnal <note>active during the night</note>; one is masculine, the other feminine; one is light, the other heavy.

2 The **exaltation** <term>a sign where a planet’s influence is strengthened</term> of any of the seven planets is said to be in that place where it substantially suffers a contrary nature from another. For example, the **Sun** <note>original symbol: ☉</note> is in **Aries** <note>original symbol: ♈</note>, which is the **fall** <term>the sign opposite a planet's exaltation, where its influence is weakened</term> of **Saturn** <note>original symbol: ♄</note>. For the Sun possesses brightness, while Saturn possesses darkness. Likewise, **Jupiter** <note>original symbol: ♃</note> is in **Cancer** <note>original symbol: ♋</note>, in which **Mars** <note>original symbol: ♂</note> falls; the one of these desires justice, while the other desires in-
<meta>catchword: justice.</meta>

---

<page-num>65</page-num>

justice. And so it is with **Mercury** <note>original symbol: ☿</note> in **Virgo** <note>original symbol: ♍</note>, which is the fall of **Venus** <note>original symbol: ♀</note>; for the one signifies science and philosophy, while the other causes cheerfulness and whatever is flavorful to the body.

3 The significance of the parts of the circle <note>the Zodiac</note>, O Great King, is based on a single element: for instance, a sign of the fiery part signifies fire; the earthy part signifies Earth; the airy signifies air; and the aquatic signifies the waters.

4 **Aries** <note>♈</note>, **Leo** <note>♌</note>, and **Sagittarius** <note>♐</note> are the hot and dry **triplicity** <term>a group of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element</term>, bitter, fiery, diurnal, and masculine; they signify **red choler** <note>original: "cholera rubra," one of the four humors, associated with a hot-tempered or "choleric" personality</note>. **Taurus** <note>♉</note>, **Virgo** <note>♍</note>, and **Capricorn** <note>♑</note> are the earthy triplicity, cold, dry, nocturnal, and feminine; they signify **black choler** <note>original: "cholera nigra," also known as melancholy</note>. **Gemini** <note>♊</note>, **Libra** <note>♎</note>, and **Aquarius** <note>♒</note> are the airy triplicity, hot, moist, sanguine, sweet, and diurnal. **Cancer** <note>♋</note>, **Scorpio** <note>♏</note>, and **Pisces** <note>♓</note> are the aquatic triplicity, cold, moist, phlegmatic, tasteless, and nocturnal.

5 The **Fortunes** <term>the benefic planets, Jupiter and Venus</term> are generous and faithful, but the **Infortunes** <term>the malefic planets, Saturn and Mars</term> are stingy and unfaithful.

6 The Fortunes will give nothing to anyone without labor. Yet the Infortunes will shorten and take away whatever they give.

7 When two Infortunes are joined together, a "perfect fortune" <note>the idea that two negatives can produce a positive outcome in specific astrological configurations</note> is made from them,

The **Angle of the Earth** <note>the Bottom of the Sky or Fourth House</note> demonstrates parts of the earth and lands, the place in which an infant is born, the hour of death, and tombs.

<meta>This page begins the first segment of Girolamo Cardano’s "Seven Segments of Astronomical Aphorisms." Having concluded the general principles of the zodiac and planetary aspects on the previous page, Cardano here establishes the philosophical and methodological foundations for the practitioner, emphasizing the difficulty of the art and the necessity of intellectual humility.</meta>

# THE FIRST
## SEGMENT.

<margin>1</margin> 1 **Life is short, art is long** <note>original: "Vita breuis, ars longa"; a famous aphorism attributed to Hippocrates, suggesting that a single lifetime is insufficient to master a complex science</note>; experience is not at our whim <note>original: "experimentum non nostri arbitrii"; meaning we cannot control the variables of experience or nature</note>, and judgment is difficult. It is necessary, therefore, not only to exercise oneself in making judgments, but also to read thoroughly the writings of others who have spoken according to reason, to discover the natural causes that are revealed by experience, and to possess the true positions of the **stars** <note>original: "syderum"</note> as well as the true progressions of their places <note>the calculated movement of planets over time</note>. Above all, one must be a lover of the truth.

<margin>2</margin> 2 The knowledge of events is perfected in three ways: *that* they will happen, *what* will eventually occur, and *when* they will happen. It is, therefore, of the greatest importance to know which of these three is being signified.

<margin>3</margin> 3 Since the arts, which are inherent to their own subjects <note>meaning sciences that deal with physical or predictable matter</note>, can promise nothing certain regarding the future, the **Astrologer** should never pronounce anything about future events in absolute terms.

63 For great men, the lowliest births <note>original: "infimæ genituræ"</note> lead toward learning; hence they are also frequently of short life, as was **Pico** <note>Giovanni Pico della Mirandola (1463–1494), a brilliant Renaissance philosopher who died at age 31.</note>. 64 It is necessary to consider the **great, middle, and minor conjunctions** <term>conjunctions; the alignment of two or more planets in the same sign. "Great" conjunctions usually refer to the meeting of Jupiter and Saturn, which occur every 20 years and cycle through the elements every 200–800 years.</term>, as well as those of the luminaries, and also the changes of the **slow-moving planets** <note>original: "Planetarum tardigradorum," referring to Saturn and Jupiter.</note> in the signs, and their encounters with the **fixed stars** <term>fixed stars; stars that do not move relative to each other, unlike "wandering stars" or planets.</term> regarding the changes of the ages.

65 The conjunction of **Saturn and Jupiter**

<column-break/>

<page-num>105</page-num>
<sig>E 5</sig>
<meta>catchword: geni-</meta>

is "minor" every 19 years, 325 days, and 19 hours. From this, the progression through the parts is 242 degrees, 59 minutes, 9 seconds; that is, through 8 signs of the **Zodiac** <note>original: "signiferi"</note>, 2 degrees, 59 minutes, and 9 seconds. And thus it proceeds within the same **triplicity** <term>triplicity; original "trigona," a group of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element (Fire, Earth, Air, or Water).</term> of the nature of the signs, as from **Aries** to **Sagittarius**, advancing by nearly three parts. From this, we recognize that the nature of the signs passes from **Fiery** into **Earthy**, then into **Airy**, and afterward into **Watery**, once ten revolutions have been completed under the same nature and quality of the signs. Therefore, they remain in the same triangle of signs for 198 common years and 236 days. Moreover, the root of the **middle conjunction** was 6 years and 67 days after **Nebuchadnezzar** <note>original: "Nabucdonofor"</note>, when a middle conjunction of Saturn and Jupiter was celebrated in 12 degrees and 23 minutes of Aries. Wherefore, a **great conjunction** occurred 53 years and 148 days before the coronation of Nebuchadnezzar, in 3 degrees and 21 minutes of Aries. Therefore, 800 years and 98 days before **Christ**, the great conjunction took its beginning, which is renewed every 794 years and 214 days.

<meta>This page continues Girolamo Cardano’s astrological aphorisms, moving from individual birth charts to the broader "mundane" astrology of religions, empires, and the history of astronomical science. Cardano compares various astronomical tables used by scholars of his time to determine planetary positions.</meta>

...moving out of a **water sign**, [the Sun] enters **Aries** ♈. Therefore, the first [ingress] is not of such a kind, for another had preceded it in **Leo**.

68 It is clear, then, that the law of **Muhammad** <note>Referring to the rise of Islam</note> began under **Aries**, following the author's birth chart <term>genitura; a birth chart or nativity</term> in **Pisces** ♓. The **Lutherans** are much the same.

69 The **Tables of Ptolemy** are superior for calculating ancient planetary motions; the **Ephemerides** <term>Ephemerides; books listing the calculated daily positions of celestial bodies</term> for current ones. The **Tables of Zacuto** <note>Abraham Zacuto (1452–1515), a Sephardic Jewish astronomer whose tables were used by Columbus and Vasco da Gama</note> and the **Tables of Elizabeth** are difficult due to their brevity and are not precise. The **Alfonsine Tables** <note>A 13th-century set of astronomical tables named after Alfonso X of Castile</note> occupy a middle ground between the Ephemerides and Ptolemy. The **Tables of Johannes de Lineriis** and **Hipparchus** have fallen out of use due to difficulty; the former because they were not exact. The **Tables of Perpetual Ephemerides** were composed with "crude skill" <note>original: "crassa minerva" - a Latin idiom for plain, unrefined work or common sense</note>. The **Tables of Johannes Blanchinus** <note>Giovanni Bianchini (1410–1469), a professor of astronomy at Ferrara</note> rely on a false assumption, as he placed the maximum longitude of the Sun at 11 degrees and 32 minutes of **Gemini** at the "root of Christ" <note>original: "Christi in radice" - the epoch or starting point for calculations centered on the birth of Christ</note>, which preceded Ptolemy’s time by more than 140 years; and many other things with which Ptolemy’s demonstrations do not agree. As for **Copernicus**, his opinion is not yet rightly understood; for he hardly seems to have said what he intended <note>Cardano lived during the early reception of Nicolaus Copernicus's heliocentric theory; many scholars struggled to reconcile it with traditional physics</note>.

70 If from **Nebuchadnezzar** to **Christ**, 747 common years and

<column-break/>

<page-num>107</page-num>

310 days are counted, according to the opinions of **Alfonso**, an error occurs in all the planets; according to the tables of **Ptolemy**, it exceeds the motion of one [degree] in **Saturn** ♄.

71 There are four things from which error arises: false reasoning, false calculation, false observation, and false numbering of times. In these last two, **Ptolemy** erred, or in one of them. It is more likely, therefore, that the observations of his predecessors were false, for in him there was no error in reasoning, nor in observation, nor in calculation. Except perhaps in the numbering of times; therefore, from Ptolemy's time onward, observations may be considered, which is why the **Alfonsine Tables** are more certain.

Therefore, the lunar month <term>lunaris mēsis</term> consists of 27 days, 9 hours, 20 minutes, and 48 seconds. The portion of one degree is 2 days, 5 hours, 54 minutes, and 3 seconds.

3. By the return of the center of the small circle <term>epicycle; in older astronomy, planets moved in small circles that themselves moved along a larger path</term> to the same place.

1 For whomsoever the lord of the <term>ascendant; the sign rising on the eastern horizon at birth</term> is afflicted by the <term>Tail of the Dragon; the South Node of the Moon, traditionally associated with loss or misfortune</term> <note>original: "cum cauda"</note>, and a <term>malefic; a planet like Saturn or Mars thought to bring difficulty</term> is in an <term>angle; one of the four most powerful points in a chart: East, West, North, or South</term>, it is inevitable that a violent death will happen to them.

2 When the lord of life is in the descending part of the sky, you shall <term>direct; a mathematical technique used to predict the timing of life events</term> it in the opposite manner.

3 When there are many <term>malefics; difficult planetary influences</term> signifying death according to the same pattern, you should not wait for the <term>cutting direction; a specific astrological timing that "cuts off" life</term>.

4 A strong <term>signifier; the planet representing a person's vitality</term> of life helps greatly in natural diseases; but in accidents, it helps little or not at all.

19 Jupiter in <term>trine; a harmonious aspect of 120 degrees</term> with the Moon grants children and riches, though more so in <term>human signs; signs depicted as humans, such as Gemini, Virgo, Libra, and Aquarius</term>.

20 When the Moon and Mercury are joined together in Taurus, the person will be studious and even learned.

21 When <term>birth charts; maps of the sky at the moment of birth</term> <note>original: "genituræ"</note> are found to be false or absurd, and do not match the things they signify, they are called "monstrous." 22 He whose Sun is in trine or in a <term>square; a challenging aspect of 90 degrees</term> with a friendly Mars, while Mars is in a square with the Moon (the lady of the <term>ascendant; the sign rising on the eastern horizon</term>) and is not friendly to her, that person will be held in hatred by both the Prince and the common people.

23 Indicators of hatred in <term>moveable signs; also known as cardinal signs, which mark the start of seasons</term> <note>original: "mobilibus"</note> relate to contempt in common or lowly matters.

25 The planet that <term>aspects; gazes upon from a specific geometric distance</term> the place of death is itself the significator of death; however, that planet necessarily also aspects the place of life. # GIROLAMO
## CARDANO’S
### Astrological
### Aphorisms
## FOURTH
## SEGMENT.

1 The <term>genitures; birth charts or nativities</term> of women are similar to those of men in matters of life <note>referring to longevity and the general course of life</note>, but they are entirely different in matters of misfortune; in character and morals, however, they hold a middle ground between the two.

2 When many planets are in the same sign, but not in the same degree, they will incline the temperament and actions toward a single type, and they will grant many successive events over the years; however, they promise nothing extraordinary.

3 The sign of Cancer is particularly powerful in our time because of the stars currently located within it, because of the <term>Great Conjunction; the meeting of Jupiter and Saturn, which occurs every 20 years and was thought to signal major historical shifts</term> which is taking place in a water sign, and because of the strength of the ruling planets.

<meta>catchword: 4 Wo-</meta>

<column-break/>

<page-num>175</page-num>

4 A woman who has Mars with the Moon in her chart cannot in any way be chaste or modest.

5 The stars found in <note>the constellation</note> Hydra, those in the tail of the Scorpion, and the head of Ophiuchus <note>original: *Serpentarij*</note>; those that share the nature of Saturn and Venus, such as the tail of the Lion <note>Denebola</note>; the conjunction of Saturn with Venus; stars of the nature of the Moon and Saturn (for which there is no specific example provided); the conjunctions of Saturn, the Moon, Venus, and Mercury; again, the conjunction of Saturn and Mars and the stars of their nature; also Mercury and Saturn and their conjunction; certain stars of the pure nature of Mars, and some of the nature of the Sun and Mars; and finally, the opposition of the <term>luminaries; the Sun and the Moon</term> and both <term>nodes; the points where the Moon's orbit crosses the ecliptic</term> (especially the <term>South Node; also called the Cauda Draconis or Dragon's Tail</term>)—all these signify poison.

6 The <term>superior planets; Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn</term>, when they first emerge from the Sun's rays <note>becoming visible in the morning sky after being "combust" or hidden by the Sun's glare</note>, make the soul noble, alert, and splendid. When they are about to enter the Sun’s rays <note>disappearing into the evening twilight</note>, they make men uncouth, fearful, and greedy. In their <term>first station; the point where a planet appears to stop before turning retrograde</term>, they make men wavering, powerful, and deceitful. In the <term>second station; the point where a planet stops before returning to direct motion</term>, they make men wavering, dejected, and weak. When they are moving retrograde at the bottom of the <term>epicycle; in the Ptolemaic system, a small circle in which a planet moves, while the center of that circle moves around a larger one</term> before their opposition to the Sun, they make men persistent, strong, and hopeful; after the opposition, they make them persistent, weak, and despairing.

7 The <term>lower planets; Mercury and Venus, the planets between Earth and the Sun</term>, when they first emerge from the Sun’s rays as morning stars <note>original: *orientales*</note>, produce weak and anxious souls; but when they first begin to appear after sunset <note>as evening stars</note>, they signify the growth of all things. When they are about to begin <term>retrogradation; the appearance of a planet moving backward in the sky</term>, they make people gloomy and wavering. When they hasten to exit that state, people are indeed weak and entirely in the power of others. While they are retrograde until they reach <term>conjunction; when two celestial bodies appear in the same place in the sky</term> with the Sun, they make people timid and not in control of themselves; but when they have already passed the Sun while still in retrograde, they make them regretful and deceptive. The Moon in <term>opposition; positioned 180 degrees apart</term> to the Sun, being then full and bright, declares perpetual contentions. But when she is <term>under the rays; combust, or hidden by the Sun's brightness</term>, she brings great losses, calamities, and the weaving of traps both for others and against oneself. In her first appearance <note>as a new crescent</note>, she makes people hopeful and changeable.

8 The status of Venus and Mercury is weak when they are western morning stars or eastern evening stars; conversely, their status is powerful when they are visible. Their influence is moderate, however, when they are western evening stars by day, or eastern morning stars by night; for in such cases they have potential, but do not bring things to completion. Between the moderate and the strong status, a planet is closer to moderate when, at night, the western evening stars have already descended below the earth; the status is closer to strong when, before dawn, the eastern stars have not—

<column-break/>

<page-num>177</page-num>

—yet ascended above the horizon of sight.

9 In full-term <term>genitures; birth charts or nativities</term>, the Moon returns to the sign that was the <term>Ascendant; the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon</term> at the moment of conception, or to its opposite sign, or to the planet with which the Moon was joined at conception, or to its aspect, or to its own proper sign. The Ascendant at birth, moreover, is the location where the Moon was at conception, or its opposite, or the location of the <term>lord; the ruling planet</term> of the conjunction <note>the New or Full Moon</note> preceding the conception.

10 If the locations of the Moon and the Ascendant of the birth and the conception were swapped, people could only be born during a few specific moments in a single day, and many people would share the exact same fate.

11 No certain limit for the time of birth is given, but most are born between the 266th and 278th day, provided they are full-term.

12 There are also solar nativities, which occur when the Sun returns to the place of the Ascendant, or to its lord, or to the place of the lord of the preceding conjunction, or returns to its own original place.

13 Saturn is rendered weak when placed in the signs of the <term>luminaries; the Sun and the Moon</term> <note>Leo and Cancer</note> and those of Mars <note>Aries and Scorpio</note>.

14 A <term>wild planet; a planet in a "feral" or wild zodiac sign such as Leo or the latter part of Sagittarius</term> <note>original: *Planeta siluester*</note> being predominant makes one desire solitude, especially if that planet is Saturn.

15 If the locations of the Moon and the Ascendant were swapped in the birth chart and the conception chart, it would be impossible for twins to be born at the same time—

16 If a similar <term>angle; one of the four cardinal points of a horoscope (Ascendant, Midheaven, etc.)</term> to the house of the lord of <term>conjunction; the alignment of planets</term> in a <term>nativity; a birth chart</term> were necessarily found according to the specific number of degrees, it would follow that many people born on the same day would necessarily share a single, identical fate.

17 **Saturn**, when well-positioned, makes people desirous of command, greedy, deceptive, experts in secrets and the law, and cruel. If, however, he is poorly positioned, he makes them envious, timid, mournful, shameless, traitors, and those who pursue even good people with unprovoked hatred.

18 A planet is said to be **badly disposed** when it is in a position contrary to its <term>dignities; the signs or places where a planet has its greatest strength</term>, entering the rays of the Sun <note>original: *radios Solis*, meaning it is becoming invisible due to the Sun's light</note>, in <term>retrograde; appearing to move backward in the sky</term>, struck by the rays of the <term>infortunes; the "malefic" planets, usually Saturn or Mars</term>, western and within 30 degrees of the Sun, falling away from an angle, joined to a powerful but "evil" fixed star, hindered, stationary, slow-moving, "wild" <note>original: *siluester*, likely referring to a planet in a bestial sign or an uncultivated state</note>, a day-planet located below the earth, or a day or night planet placed contrary to its proper sect above the earth, being an evening planet when it should be morning (or vice versa), or diminished in its light.

19 Planets are said to **communicate** when both commonly rule over a single place, or when the one who rules aspects another, or is joined to it by a few degrees, or when the ruling planet gives its power to another, or when light is carried from a lighter

<column-break/>

<page-num>179</page-num>
<sig>H 6</sig>

planet to it. If the joined or aspecting planet has no <term>dignity; standing or power</term> in that place, the person will be inconsistent and disorganized. This is indeed seen even if the planets ruling together are not of contrary natures, such as **Saturn** and **Venus**, **Mars** and the **Moon**, or **Jupiter**, the **Sun**, and the **Moon**. They also communicate when another planet rules in the place of the primary ruler. Therefore, he who rules alone should be solitary and in his own dignities.

20 A planet is said to be **assimilated** whenever it is in the dignities and under the <term>aspect; the geometric relationship between planets</term> of another.

21 When two planets rule together, the judgment will be a mixture of what both signify. However, when the lord itself is assimilated to another, it will obtain a certain primary power.

22 Whenever **Mercury** is closest to the **Moon**, the person born will be similar to them in every respect.

23 **Saturn**, if he is assimilated to **Jupiter** and well-disposed, will make the person born very prudent, high-minded, quiet, a philosopher, and a minister of a kingdom. If poorly disposed, however, he makes them stubborn without reason, devoted to vain arts, solitary, tedious, difficult, and unfortunate.

24. If **Saturn** is likened to **Mars** <note>This "likening" usually refers to an aspect—a specific geometric angle—between the two planets in a birth chart</note> and is well-disposed, the person will be stubborn, cruel, a traitor, reckless, talkative, quick to anger, and a flatterer. He pursues gods, men, and princes with hatred. He is a cutthroat who will be moved by no prayers or reasons; a gambler, a braggart, immoderate in all things, yet hardworking, wretched, harmful, criminal, and prone to <term>incest; in this context, it often broadly referred to any socially or religiously prohibited sexual act</term>. If he is badly disposed, these traits will be even stronger, and he will be a coward, a thief and a brigand, impious, and altogether unhappy.

25. The results will be almost the same if **Mars** is likened to **Saturn**, except that he will retain more of the properties of Mars. For he will be bolder, more quick-tempered, and headlong, but less of a traitor, deceiver, miser, or envious person.

26. If **Saturn** is well-disposed and likened to **Venus**, he will be a hater of women and will scorn beautiful things. Nevertheless, he will fear God; he is a man of secret counsel, peaceful, modest, a diviner, jealous, and tedious, with a moderate amount of filthiness. If badly disposed, he is a drunkard, defiled by every sexual vice. He will desire not only to perform but to submit to shameful acts <note>original: *pati non solum agere cupiet*, a reference to passive and active roles in sexual encounters</note>; he will even be inclined toward the mating of beasts. Thinking of things even worse than these, he is a slanderer, most envious, a sorcerer, filthy, idle, and lazy,

37 **Jupiter**, when he is likened to the **Sun**, makes men generous (though with some tenacity), splendid, strong, just, pious, faithful, wise, magnificent, great-souled, and most fortunate; finally, he makes them divine, well-dressed, polished, clean, and modest.

38 If **Jupiter** should appear similar to **Venus**, the person born will be very pious, loving, grateful, just, humane, splendid, munificent, polished, clean, adorned, and most generous. He will be a seeker of jokes and food, honest, faithful, and observant of his kindred; he will love his friends and be devoted to physical love according to the law; he will be a lover of his children and wife, of sound mind, and will cherish learning and the sciences more than he possesses them; he will be of a pure soul, merciful, and will even undergo evils willingly for the sake of God.

39 If **Jupiter** is likened to **Mercury**, he will be skilled in all sciences, of good natural talent, good counsel, and good morals; he will be a benefactor who loves associations <note>original: "collegia," referring to guilds, societies, or organized groups</note> and will cherish his friends and blood-relations; he will possess riches and honors, and will manage the affairs of Princes. However, he will be of a changeable character, cunning, and deceptive.

82 **Ludovico Riccio** <note>original: "Ludouicus Rigius," a 16th-century Italian astrologer and physician</note> said that the **Moon** joined to **Mars** in the air signs <note>Gemini, Libra, and Aquarius</note> signifies a blow or strike from a person, especially when in **Gemini**. ## FIFTH
### SEGMENT.

1 For whomever the **Moon**, the mistress of the **ascendant** <term>ascendant|The zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth, considered the most important point for physical health</term>, is beneath the earth with the **Tail of the Lion** <note>original: "cauda Leonis". Specifically the star Denebola.</note>, and the **Sun** is at the **Head of the Virgin** <note>original: "Virginis capite". Specifically the star Zavijava.</note> in the **sixth house** <term>sixth house|The section of a birth chart traditionally associated with illness, service, and small animals</term>, and **Saturn** or **Mars** is in its **dignity** <term>dignity|A position in the zodiac where a planet's power is strengthened or harmonized</term> in the angle of the **seventh house** <term>seventh house|The house of marriage and open enemies, located on the western horizon</term>, perpetual weakness will be present.

2 The births of siblings often have the same **ascendant**, because the "place of children" in the parents' charts often remains the same.

3 Whomever has **Venus** in the same part in which **Saturn** or **Mars** occupy **Gemini**, these people suffer from every kind of **unchastity** <note>original: "incestu". In Renaissance Latin, this term was broader than the modern "incest"; it referred to any grave sexual sin or the violation of religious vows of chastity.</note> toward boys and holy virgins.

4 The **Lord of the second house** <term>second house|The area of a horoscope associated with personal finances and possessions</term> located in the second indicates wealth from regular income; in the third house, it signifies wealth from relatives or through travel. Therefore, every **planet** in its own house easily demonstrates something—whether good or bad.

5 Every hindrance of an evil thing is a good thing; every hindrance of a good thing is an evil thing. <note>In astrology, if a "malefic" planet like Saturn is blocked, the outcome is positive for the subject.</note>

6 The return of light to a better planet is good.

7 Effects are equal whether three **significators** <term>significator|A planet that represents a specific person or area of life in a chart</term> are hindered at once, or if one is hindered by three others.

8 **Mercury** in **Pisces** causes an impediment of the tongue and absurdity in speech; such people say something other than what they have conceived in their minds. The same is true if **Pisces** is the **ascendant**.

10 Whoever is born at the exact noon of an **equinox** will become great by this fact alone.

12 Women for whom the **ascendant**, the **Moon**, **Mars**, **Venus**, and **Mercury** are all in **bicorporeal signs** <term>bicorporeal|Also known as "mutable" signs—Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, and Pisces—which were thought to represent instability of character</term> are of the worst morals.

**109** When several children achieve the same fortune: if it happens in childhood, it occurs through the parents' **birth chart** <term>birth chart|original: "genitura" — the arrangement of the stars at the moment of birth, believed to determine one's fate</term> by itself. **112** **Albubather** <note>Albubather (Abu Bakr al-Hasan ibn al-Khasib) was a 9th-century Persian astrologer whose works on nativities were highly influential in the Renaissance.</note> said, and I say rightly, that when all the planets are in the **sixth, eighth, or twelfth houses**, the newborn will not be nourished. <note>In traditional astrology, these three "dark" houses were considered malefic and suggested the infant would not survive to be raised.</note>

from the **equinox**; it is of another kind in the world, which is the return to the same **fixed star**; and it is of yet another kind in birth charts, which is the return to the original position, adding however that part of the **ecliptic** <term>ecliptic|the circular path of the Sun across the sky as seen from Earth</term> which the Sun can travel in one natural day. <note>A "natural day" refers to a full 24-hour period.</note>

**115** The year and the day are similar. We call it a "day" when the **Sun** returns to a point it has already traveled. The same must be established for the "year": for it is the return and passage of the parts which the Sun completes in one natural day.

**116** When the **Moon** is in conjunction with or in opposition to the **Sun**, she is in the **apsis** <term>apsis|the point in an orbit where a celestial body is at its maximum or minimum distance from the center of its motion</term> of her **eccentric**. <note>Traditional astronomy used "eccentrics" (circles whose centers are offset from Earth) to explain the varying speeds of planets.</note> Therefore, when she is in **square** <note>A square is a 90-degree angle between two planets, usually considered a point of tension.</note> to the Sun, she is best positioned.

But these do not behave equally. The **Moon** is in the opposite of the eccentric apsis and in the opposite of the apsis of the small circle. For she is the mistress of the elements. # GIROLAMO
## CARDANO’S
### Astrological
### Aphorisms
#### SIXTH
#### SEGMENT.

1 When, in the <term>revolution: also known as a solar return, this is a chart cast for a person's birthday to predict events for the coming year</term> of a person whose sole indicator of life is already weakened, the good planets <note>the "benefics," typically Jupiter and Venus</note> are <term>combust: an astrological condition where a planet is so close to the Sun that its influence is overwhelmed or "burnt up" by the Sun's light</term> in a location other than the <term>ascendant: the sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth</term>, and the <term>malefics: "infortunae," referring to the challenging planets Saturn and Mars</term> aspect the Sun while being above the earth, and also aspect the ascendant and the Moon (or if the Moon is below the earth): even without any <term>direction: a complex mathematical technique used to time major life events</term>, that person will undoubtedly die in that year.

2 When Saturn and Mars aspect one another, and the <term>luminaries: the Sun and the Moon</term> are in the sixth, eighth, or twelfth houses <note>these houses were traditionally associated with illness, death, and hidden burdens</note>, the person born will lead a miserable life due to an incurable disease and will live in sadness.

3 When the malefics dominate, they make people

<column-break/>

wicked; when they are powerful, they cause misfortunes.

4 If the <term>birth chart: "genitura," the map of the heavens at the moment of birth</term> indicates a weak vitality, and three planets are joined together at the same time in the revolution, a danger of disease looms, especially if they are in the sixth house.

5 When the Moon is in the <term>midheaven: the highest point of the chart, representing career and public reputation</term> in Capricorn, and Saturn or Mars is at the <term>bottom of the sky: "imum coeli," the lowest point of the chart, representing roots and the end of life</term>, the person born will be infamous. If Mars is in Taurus and the Moon in Scorpio in the same way, this will be even worse and more permanent, and there will be many hardships throughout their entire life.

6 Do not praise the intellect of someone who has Mercury in Taurus or Virgo in the west <note>meaning Mercury sets after the Sun</note>, and much less in Capricorn, even though it may seem excellent; unless it is joined with Jupiter, or Venus, or the Moon, or a fixed star of their nature.

7 When the Moon is in Aries, it grants a good but changeable intellect.

8 Lameness, cross-eyedness, leg deformities, and other calamities are caused by an afflicted Moon, because it triggers <term>convulsions: "convulsionem," which could refer to spasms or neurological seizures</term>.

9 True motions <note>the actual, observable positions of the planets</note> perfect the actions; but mean motions <note>the calculated average speed of a planet</note> are like the patterns of those actions.

10 When the Sun aspects any of the superior planets <note>Saturn, Jupiter, or Mars</note>, consider that same condition of that aspect in the half-revolu- <note>original: "reuolutio-"</note>

22 To attain a kingdom, two out of these three are always necessary: the connection of family through succession, some good found in the **birth chart**, and its compatibility with the kingdom in question.

23 It is easy, therefore, to understand why a kingdom is more easily and more frequently lost through succession than one gained by one's own strength.

24 The more specific significance of the **lord of the triplicity** <note>original: 'domini trigoni'; the planet that rules a set of three signs of the same element</note> concerns the years of infancy; that of the **house** concerns the body; that of the **exaltation** concerns fortune and power; and that of the **terms** <note>original: 'termini'; specific segments of a zodiac sign ruled by different planets</note> concerns the character of the mind.

25 When, in adulthood, the **yearly return** <note>original: 'reuolutio'; a chart cast for the moment the Sun returns to its birth position</note> has **Venus** in **sextile** aspect <note>an aspect of 60 degrees, usually considered harmonious</note> to **Mercury**, which was joined with it in the same place in the birth chart, the native will be wonderfully vexed by sexual fantasies; but if they are joined where they were previously in sextile, he will obtain his beloved mistress in that year.

164 When Mars strikes Jupiter from a square <term>square: an aspect of 90 degrees, traditionally considered challenging or tense</term> or an opposition <term>opposition: an aspect of 180 degrees, indicating direct conflict</term>, the children of the native will for the most part perish by a violent death; this is especially certain if, along with this, Mars or Jupiter is the lord of the fifth or tenth house <note>the fifth house traditionally governs children, while the tenth can represent their social standing or the "outcome" of the parents' legacy</note>.

165 The tenth house is a place of children; if neither the Sun nor a malefic <term>malefic: "infortuna," a planet like Saturn or Mars traditionally thought to bring misfortune</term> is in it or rules it; after that, the eleventh house is considered, then the fifth; then the positions of Jupiter, the Moon, and Venus when they act as rulers. ## SEVENTH
## SEGMENT.

¶ 1 For any person who has no planet above the earth <note>i.e., in the visible sky above the horizon at the moment of birth</note>, nor any planet in the first hour of its rising, it is impossible for them not only to live a long life, but also to achieve anything truly remarkable.

2 One who has the Moon in the sixth house <term>sixth house: the region of the sky traditionally associated with illness, burdens, and daily labor</term> in aspect to a malefic planet <note>original: "infortunae aspectu," meaning a challenging angle from Saturn or Mars</note> will suffer from an incurable disease; this is even more certain if the Moon is the ruler of the ascendant <term>ascendant: the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at birth, which represents the physical body</term>.

3 Regarding illnesses, count as many days as it takes for the Moon to return to the same point in its circle of position; for in this way days are also counted for the Sun.

4 The calculation of "critical days" <note>days when a patient's condition is expected to shift significantly</note> reaches fully to the eightieth day, but also to the hundredth and the hundred and twentieth, because a beginning is counted as a whole.

hundredth, and the hundred and twentieth, because a beginning is counted as a whole.

5 Therefore, as many times as the Moon, passing from point to point, has traversed the highest orb and returned to the same circle of position, the Sun is said to effect the same—though this necessarily happens in a shorter relative time.

6 When Saturn is in Libra and Jupiter is in Cancer, then great changes will occur in the world <note>original: "magnae in mundo mutationes contingent"</note>.

7 When the Moon is in a watery sign <term>watery sign: Cancer, Scorpio, or Pisces</term> during winter and is joined to a retrograde planet <term>retrograde: a planet that appears to move backward in the sky from the perspective of Earth</term>, there will be rain or snow, especially if it is joined to Saturn.

8 You should not seek evidence for a plurality of wives—in societies where only one wife is legally permitted—merely from a gathering of planets or from common signs <term>common signs: also called "mutable" signs (Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces), which often symbolize multiplicity</term>. Rather, look for this if the Moon’s rays or its physical body apply to planets at vigorous ages, provided that signs of the deaths of previous wives are also present.

9 You can understand the strength of a wife from the state which the Moon reaches through direction <term>direction: a predictive technique where planets are "moved" forward in time to determine the timing of life events</term> at that time; the same principle applies to children and younger siblings.

10 For parents and elder siblings, however, judge from the state of the significators <term>significator: the specific planet or point in the chart representing a person or topic</term> in a preceding position, counting back through as many years as they preceded the time of birth.

50 Cold increases moisture by accident <note>In Aristotelian physics, "by accident" means an indirect result, such as cold condensing vapor into water</note>.

65 Out of the three <term>openings of the gates</term> <note>original: "portarum apertionib⁹"; a technical astrological term referring to specific planetary aspects that "open" the atmosphere to allow wind or rain to flow</note>, the configuration belonging to **Jupiter** and **Mercury** produces the most wind; that of **Mars** and **Venus** produces water; and that of **Saturn** and the <term>luminaries</term> <note>the Sun and Moon</note> produces hail, snow, and cold.

66 Calamities do not occur unless the <term>malefics</term> <note>original: "infortuniis"; the planets Saturn and Mars, traditionally associated with hardship</note> are dominant; for this reason, floods cannot occur when the planets are in **Pisces** or **Cancer** [without their influence].

71 One must also observe the <term>heliacal</term> <note>rising or setting just before or after the sun, making a star briefly visible on the horizon</note> risings and settings of the brighter stars; for it rarely happens that droughts and diseases do not flourish during the rising of the **Dog Star** <note>original: "caniculæ"; the star Sirius, associated with the "dog days" of summer</note>, or that rains do not fall during the setting of **Arcturus**.

83 Each of the <term>superior planets</term> <note>the planets further from the Sun than Earth: Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn</note>, but especially **Mars**, is a little further from the Sun when in opposition to it than when in conjunction; therefore, they receive almost equal light in both positions.

84 As for the **Moon**, if we assume what **Ptolemy** <note>the foundational 2nd-century astronomer and astrologer</note> asserts—that its diameter has a ratio of 10 to 187 compared to the Sun's diameter, and a ratio of height roughly 1 to 19, and that its height relative to the Earth's radius is as 59 to 1—then in <term>conjunctions</term> <note>the New Moon, when the Sun and Moon are aligned</note>

85 When the **Moon** receives more light, it dries things out; when it receives less light, it brings moisture.

89 But if, along with these conditions, **Mars** is in opposition to the **Moon** and **Venus**, and **Saturn** casts its <term>aspect</term> <note>a specific geometric angle from one planet to another</note> upon them, the land that is submerged will thereafter be considered part of the sea.

92 If, therefore, near the **equinoxes**, the **Moon** in **Cancer** has excited the tide of a full moon or a new moon, while **Saturn** is in <term>opposition</term> <note>planets 180 degrees apart</note> or in <term>square</term> <note>planets 90 degrees apart</note>, the sea will swell and flood the neighboring lands; and even more so if **Saturn** is with **Arcturus**, or the **Moon** with **Orion**.

93 On individual days, since the water flows for six hours and ebbs for as many, a portion of the day is added according to the Moon’s progress—so that roughly a quarter of an hour is added to the six hours. When the **Moon** <term>applies</term> <note>moves toward an aspect with</note> to **Saturn** or **Venus**, the tide is increased; but the ebb is increased when it applies to **Mars** or **Jupiter**. The Moon itself creates a tide from its rising until it reaches the <term>midheaven</term> <note>original: "caeli cor," the highest point in the sky</note>, where it pauses a little, and the stirred waters are also increased; but they are carried back toward the seas when the Moon has finished its journey and reaches roughly the beginning of the **sixth house** <note>an astrological division of the sky below the western horizon</note>.
