100 **Full moons** are usually cold in the summer, but more temperate in the winter, unless the power of **Saturn** offers resistance. However, **new moons** usually bring hot nights in the summer and very cold nights in the winter.

101 The **Etesian winds** <note>original: "Eteſiæ"; these are strong, periodic Mediterranean winds</note> blow from the North in the Black Sea <note>original: "Ponto"</note>, from the East in Africa and Spain, and from the South in other places; they begin in the morning at the third hour of the day and cease in the evening. During the **winter solstice** <note>original: "Bruma"</note>, they are mild and usually blow for only a few days.

102 To us, the Eastern and Southern winds bring rains. The Northern winds <note>original: "boreales"</note> and the West wind <note>original: "Favonii"</note> bring clear skies. However, different winds act differently in other places.

103 The rising of the **Pleiades** <note>original: "Vergiliarum"</note> stirs up the east wind. The West wind <note>original: "Favonius"</note> follows its own beginning when the **Sun** is in the 25th degree of **Aquarius**, and it lasts for about nine days. But eight days before the rising of the **Dog Star** <note>original: "caniculæ," referring to Sirius</note>, the "precursor" north winds <note>original: "prodromi aquilones"</note> come forth; they are followed by others two days later. The **Etesian winds** last for forty days, during which the power of the Dog Star also roughly persists. Before the setting of **Arcturus**, the south winds blow. The Northwest wind <note>original: "Corus"</note> blows at the **autumnal equinox**. The setting of the **Pleiades**, however, stirs up the wintry North wind.

109 When trees are in bloom, they are most affected by the injuries of the sky, for they are then like women in childbirth; however, when they produce fruit, they are like those breastfeeding and nursing.

171 When the **Moon** is in her middle **conjunction** <note>original: "conjunctione"; the alignment of two celestial bodies</note> with the **Sun**, she holds one hundred parts of a **small circle** <term>epicycle; in the Ptolemaic system, a small circle whose center moves along the circumference of a larger one</term>, not only with the center of the Sun, but also with the small circles of **Venus** and **Mercury**, from which wonderful effects follow. It is clear, moreover, that the center of the small circle possesses its own powers.

172 Before the 40th year, the **significator of life** <note>the planet or point in a birth chart, such as the Ascendant or Sun, that represents a person's physical vitality</note> is rarely shaken, as the law of nature resists it; however, for those whose only significator is shaken, it is impossible for them to reach their sixtieth year.

173 Whoever uses these precepts correctly should know that they will be able to predict future events for the most part; they will do what we have done, and far greater things, provided they have correctly understood that the **heavens** are a **divine instrument**.

->THE END.<-

# VARIOUS
## APHORISMS
### BY AN UNKNOWN AUTHOR.

1 One who is naturally well-disposed toward **Astrology** will certainly pronounce more accurate judgments.

2 Diverse effects are drawn from the **stars** according to the different dispositions of **matter**; therefore, the Astrologer must very carefully examine the different natures and qualities of the subjects receiving these influences.

3 Since matter always determines **form**, it happens that we, through our own **wicked actions** <note>original: "pravas operationes"; suggesting that human behavior can trigger the negative potentials of a star's influence</note>, freely determine the stars to bring us harm.

4 The forms by which the celestial bodies act are called **images**, to which inferior forms <note>earthly things</note> are subject. These are many, found in the **signs**, **decans** <term>divisions of a zodiac sign into three parts of ten degrees each, each ruled by a different planet</term>, and **degrees**; they are also in individual stars separately, and in many together.

5 There are many sensible **images** of the **eighth Sphere** <note>the "Firmament" or sphere of the fixed stars that sits beyond the seven planets</note>, and many are created daily by the **Planets** themselves; all of these must be considered by the Astrologer. They have

# Acute Illnesses by the Motion of the Moon

...the body, or the significator of the disease, or if it is in a northern sign, the patient must be carefully guarded, lest seized by madness <note>original: "furore"; referring to a state of delirium or acute psychiatric distress</note> they bring death upon themselves.

208 If the planet signifying the patient **applies** <note>moves toward a geometric aspect</note> to a **Fortune** <term>Fortune; a "benefic" or helpful planet like Jupiter or Venus</term>, and then to an **Infortune** <term>Infortune; a "malefic" or harmful planet like Saturn or Mars</term>, a relapse of the disease will occur for the patient.

209 The disease will be severe if, in that year, the **profectional signs** <term>Profection; a technique where the chart is advanced by one sign per year to determine yearly influences</term> of the **Hylegial places** <term>Hyleg; the specific point or planet in a birth chart that acts as the "giver of life"</term> are afflicted.

210 At the **decumbiture** <term>Decumbiture; the moment a patient first takes to their bed, used to cast a chart for the course of the illness</term>, you shall consider the motion of the Planet causing the disease through certain numbers of degrees, so that you may know the turning points of the disease.

211 A **chronic disease** is regulated by the motion of the **Sun**, or the planet causing the disease.

<column-break/>

212 The **critical points** <term>Critical points; specific times during an illness when the patient's condition is expected to change significantly</term> in acute diseases are accelerated or delayed according to the slow or fast motion of the Moon.

213 Manifest **crises** <note>original: "crises"; the turning points where a patient either begins to recover or declines toward death</note> occur if the Moon reaches a sign that is contrary in both qualities to the sign it was in at the beginning of the illness. <note>For example, if the illness began with the Moon in a hot/moist sign, the crisis occurs when it hits a cold/dry sign.</note>

214 It is necessary for the critical point to be when the Moon reaches its **square** <term>Square; an aspect of 90 degrees, often associated with tension or challenge</term> or **opposition** [180 degrees]: But it also happens when it reaches the nearest **term** <term>Term; also called "Bounds," these are five unequal subdivisions of each zodiac sign ruled by different planets</term> which is of a contrary quality to the sign where the Moon was at the start of the illness.

215 If the Moon, reaching a **critical angle**, finds benevolent planets and the patient is meant to recover, a "completed crisis" occurs; if they are meant to die, the crisis will be deceptive <note>meaning the patient may seem to improve briefly before failing</note>.

216 In a lethal disease, if the Moon reaching a critical angle finds harmful planets, the crisis will be bad, but certain.

217 If in a lethal disease the Moon at a critical angle finds harmful planets, a bad crisis occurs, but it is untrustworthy.

218 If a crisis occurs in a **violent sign** <note>signs like Aries, Scorpio, or Capricorn</note>, and at the critical angle the Moon beholds **Mars**, **Saturn**, or **Mercury** (if it is acting like them), the crisis will happen with savage symptoms <note>original: "sævis accidentibus"</note>.

# APHORISMS
## ASTROLOGICAL

->*By an Unknown Author*<-

1 A specific planetary arrangement <term>constellation; here referring to a particular configuration of planets at a specific moment</term> brings into reality at its proper time those events which were previously indicated by a more general and superior arrangement. <note>The author suggests a hierarchy of influence, where broad "universal" cycles set the stage for specific events triggered by daily planetary movements.</note>

2 A more powerful astrological cause overrides the indications of a weaker, opposing cause.

3 A person <note>original: "Natus," literally "the one born," referring to the subject of a birth chart</note> will attain the highest authority and status if, at the moment of their birth, Jupiter and Mars bestow their power upon Saturn. <note>In traditional astrology, Saturn represents structure and time; receiving the "virtue" or strength of Jupiter (growth) and Mars (action) suggests a person who can build a lasting legacy through disciplined ambition.</note>

4 Having all or most planets positioned in the **angles** <term>angles; the four most powerful points in a horoscope: the Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, and Imum Coeli</term> makes a person's life and actions highly distinguished and famous. However, if all the planets are **cadent** <term>cadent; houses that "fall away" from the angles, traditionally considered weaker and less capable of producing public action</term>, the person’s entire life will be obscure, and they will be listless in their endeavors.

5 If the planets in a birth chart do not "see" one another through **aspects** <term>aspects; specific geometric relationships between planets, such as a square or trine, through which they exert influence on each other</term>, or only do so through minor ones, the person's life will be fragmented, and their various actions will seem disconnected from one another.

6 An **impediment** or **defect** in the eyes will be suffered by the Native <note>original: *Natus*, the person born under the specific astrological chart being analyzed</note>, if either of the **luminaries** <term>luminaries; the Sun and the Moon, the two primary light-givers in astrology</term> is afflicted by a malefic planet <note>original: *malefico*, typically referring to Mars or Saturn, which were thought to cause harm</note> while positioned with a nebulous star <note>nebulous stars refer to clusters like the Pleiades or Praesepe, which traditional astrology often associated with eye problems or blindness</note>, especially if this occurs in an unlucky area of the chart.

7 The **order** and meaning of the "houses" <term>houses; the twelve divisions of an astrological chart representing different areas of life, such as career, health, or home</term> can also be applied to the zodiac signs themselves, starting from the "House" <note>the sign ruled by a specific planet</note> of any planet based on that planet's specific meanings and power.

8 **Planets** vary their meanings through every individual degree of the zodiac in the same way that they vary their meanings as they move through the different Houses of the chart.

9 A **Planet** that is influenced by both a "fortune" <term>fortune; a benefic planet like Jupiter or Venus that brings growth or harmony</term> and a "misfortune" <term>misfortune; a malefic planet like Saturn or Mars</term> at the same time will act according to both influences. However, if it is overwhelmed by multiple misfortunes, it will be considered entirely unlucky and will produce purely harmful effects.

10 **Conjunction** <note>planets in the same spot</note> and **opposition** <note>planets 180 degrees apart</note> are separated by a straight diametrical line, and the two intermediate **squares** <note>planets 90 degrees apart</note> are also diametrically opposed to one another. Therefore, the squares are perpendicular to the conjunction and opposition, and vice versa. Because of this geometric relationship, these four configurations are considered very powerful in their operations.

<column-break/>

11 Even **numbers** are likened to the cold elements <note>Water and Earth</note> and therefore to death—especially the fourth and the eighth. The fourth is the square of two, while the eighth is a "cube" <note>2x2x2</note>, which signifies the completion of a finished work or the end of a perfected body.

12 **In** the changes of the elements, the growth of fruits, and the various parts of the body, the "natural significators" <note>planets that naturally represent physical things, like Venus for beauty or Mars for blood</note> hold the greatest power. However, regarding the inclinations of the mind, the "special significators" are most powerful. In both cases, "accidental significators" <note>planets that gain temporary importance due to their specific position in a single chart</note> can play a role.

13 **Fixed stars** that are not joined to planets have much smaller effects than the planets themselves; however, when they are joined to planets, they produce the most intense and violent effects.

14 We say that the **influences** <note>original: *influxus*, the "flowing in" of celestial power</note> that change the physical elements also alter us. Yet, there are many effects produced by the Stars and the Heavens upon animals and other composite beings that do not change the elements themselves. Thus, the Heavens work upon us both mediately <note>through the physical environment</note> and immediately <note>directly upon the spirit or soul</note>.

15 **Celestial bodies** are "equivocal causes" <note>original: *causæ equiuocę*; a philosophical term for a cause that produces an effect different from its own nature. For example, the same Sun melts wax but hardens clay.</note>, which is why a human being can freely submit themselves to either this or that celestial impression. <note>This aphorism argues for human free will: while the stars provide an impulse, the human mind decides how to react to it.</note>

78. A human being, driven by their sensory passions, is accustomed to obeying their desires. 79. Because the intellect, in its non-reflective operations, depends on a bodily organ <note>referring here to the brain</note> upon which the stars act directly, the stars therefore act indirectly upon the intellect. # GIROLAMO MANFREDI
## Most Illustrious Philosopher, Physician, and Astrologer.
### *Regarding Physicians and the Sick.*

1. Although Medicine is a most perfect science in its own right; nevertheless, a Physician is not perfect in his practice without the study of **Astrology**. <note>In the Renaissance, medicine and astrology were deeply intertwined; doctors believed the movements of planets directly influenced human health and the efficacy of treatments.</note>

2. O, how great an error it is for a skilled Physician to be utterly lacking in knowledge of the Stars! For without it, neither the administration of medicines, nor **bloodletting** <term>bloodletting (phlebotomy); a medical practice involving the withdrawal of blood to balance the body's "humors" or fluids, which was strictly timed according to lunar cycles</term>, nor any other part of his work can be performed correctly. Furthermore, neither the nature of a disease, nor the end <note>original: *finem*; referring to the prognosis or the final outcome of the illness</note> it is destined to reach, can be perfectly understood without the observation of the Stars. It is for this reason that the most ancient of the Egyptians joined the science of Astrology to the science of Medicine, so that both

He will be a **good Physician** in whose Nativity <note>A "Nativity" is a birth chart or horoscope calculated for the moment of a person's birth.</note> **Mars** and **Venus** are joined bodily, or by some favorable aspect. Likewise **Venus** and **Mercury**. 4. Truly, the error of an **Astrologer** will be great in questions regarding the sick when the **seventh house** and its Lord <note>In medical astrology (horary), the seventh house and its ruling planet represent the physician.</note> are afflicted; therefore, you should delay the questioning, or do not speak upon it for fear of error.

5. 43 When the **Ascendant** <term>the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon</term> and the **Moon** are afflicted <note>original: *damnati*; placed in a difficult position or aspected by "malefic" planets like Mars or Saturn</note>, but their Lords <term>the planets that rule those signs</term> are safe, the sickness will be in the body and not in the spirit. 76 The **Rule of the Indians** <note>referring to Indo-Persian astrological traditions</note> is as follows: count the years from the hour of birth until the beginning of the sickness. For one who stayed in the womb for nine months, multiply the aforementioned years by five and divide by nine. If the person stayed in the womb for seven months, take one day for each year and divide by seven. 77 In diseases, there are certain days and hours in which their changes toward good or evil are declared

quickly; these are **critical days** <term>from the Greek 'krisis,' a turning point in a disease</term>, or days of "battle." From this, it follows that the seventh, fourteenth, and twentieth (or twenty-first) days are called "critical" by physicians. The **indicative days**, however—by which judgment is taken for the critical days regarding health, death, or the danger of death—are the midpoints of the squares. Therefore, the fourth, eleventh, and seventeenth days are counted as indicative. Here, the square or **aspect** is taken by the **direct circle** <note>calculated by the movement of the celestial sphere rather than simple zodiacal degrees</note> and not by equal degrees; and this holds if the illness proceeds according to its natural quality and no error occurs that disturbs the patient. If, however, you find an **Infortune**, signify an adverse change, unless that Infortune is contrary to the nature of the sickness and the Fortune is similar to it. And the **Moon** in these angles always signifies **acute** <note>sharp and fast-moving</note> diseases, and the **Sun** signifies **prolonged** ones.

17 The most well-known meetings of the stars are these: the **Moon** with the fixed stars, the **Moon** with the **Sun**, the **Moon** with **Saturn** and other planets; the **Sun** with the fixed stars and with the planets; **Mercury** with the **Sun** and with the fixed stars, and afterwards with other planets. **Venus** with these same stars. Finally, the meetings of **Saturn** and **Jupiter** with the rest are hardly known; those of **Saturn** indeed with **Jupiter** because of the slowness of their motion; those of **Mars**, however, because of the small size of the orbit in which it is carried; today, however, the meetings of the stars are observed and noted with more accurate study.

18 The promises of the stars are diminished, increased, and overturned by many causes: such as the nature of the seed <note>The biological makeup or lineage of the person</note>, homeland, education, habit, and those things which follow and depend upon these.

29 The speed of motion in the **Moon** is to be considered most carefully, as it has the greatest effect; next are **Mercury** and **Venus**. For the speed of motion in the "superior" planets <note>The planets further from the Sun: Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn</note> does not have as much influence as it does in the "inferior" ones <note>The planets closer to Earth: Moon, Mercury, and Venus</note>.

30 The state of the planets must be considered not only in relation to the **Sun**, but also to the **Moon**. **Jupiter**, along with the Sun and the Moon, is the author of fertility.

31 All stars are endowed with both their own light and the light of the Sun; the **Moon** indeed has more from another source <note>original: *plus alieno*, referring to reflected sunlight</note>, while the others have their own, or an equal amount, but very little of it.

32 None of the superior planets can be very moist, nor can any of the inferior ones be very dry.

33 The **Moon** and **Mercury** produce the most unstable people, because neither of them ever rests.

34 Because the motion of the Moon is perpetually visible, the instability of "lunatics" <note>original: *lunaticorum*; literally "those affected by the moon"</note> is known to everyone; for this reason, it is even called "folly."

35 The instability of **Mercury** is uncertain and not so obvious; therefore it is called "craftiness" <note>original: *calliditas*</note> and has the appearance of wisdom, although it is not true wisdom, but rather a certain unstable and deceitful nature.

45 Large **fixed stars** are more effective; the small ones are weak.

46 The stars act through their light, and their power is exactly as it appears in its final effect.

47 Fixed stars, because they are furthest from the Earth and move very slowly by their own motion, do not reach the Earth with their power directly; instead, their influence is mixed with that of the other planets.

48 Fixed stars that are closer to the <term>Ecliptic line</term> <note>The apparent path of the Sun across the sky</note> transmit their powers to us through the benefit of the planets that are joined with them.

49 A fixed star of a similar nature to a planet it is paired with produces the most obvious effects; when paired with a contrary planet, the effects are very obscure; with a dissimilar planet of another kind, the effects are uncertain and can hardly be recognized until after they have happened.

50 Fixed stars joined with the **Sun** have the greatest effects on one's life and honors; with the **Moon**, they affect fortune; then follow their effects with Jupiter, Saturn, Mars, Venus, and Mercury.

51 Planets in opposition <note>180 degrees apart</note> and in <term>Squares</term> <note>90 degrees apart</note> to the Sun, if they are at those exact points, behave as they do at the first point of their first station <note>The point where a planet appears to stop before turning retrograde</note>: they are as much hotter as they are moister. Before this point, they are moister than they are hot; after, they are drier than they are hot. At the exact point of opposition, they are as much hotter as they are drier. But at that moment, it is as if they added nothing of heat or dryness; immediately after, they become dry and cold. Thus, dryness begins to increase until the midpoint of the space leading to the second station; from there, dryness diminishes, while coldness increases until the midpoint between the second station and its <term>occultation</term> <note>original: *occultationem*; when the planet disappears behind the Sun's light</note>. There it finally settles and becomes weakest.

However, in matters of life and the affections of the soul and body, the Ascendant is stronger because it is more personal to the individual. After these follow the houses in this order: 7th, 11th, 9th, 8th, 2nd, and 6th.

# THE HUNDRED APHORISMS
## OF B E T H E M.

1. I shall begin this book regarding the customs in the judgments of the stars.
2. Know that when planets are <term>retrograde</term> <note>Appearing to move backward from Earth's perspective.</note>, they are like a sick man: dazed and anxious.
3. A <term>cadent</term> <note>From the Latin "cadens" (falling); a planet in a house that "falls away" from the powerful angles, specifically the 3rd, 6th, 9th, or 12th houses.</note> planet is truly like a dead man who has no movement.
4. A <term>combust</term> <note>A planet so close to the Sun that its influence is thought to be "burned up" or hidden by the Sun's light.</note> planet is like a captive—imprisoned and shamed, and without power.
5. A planet standing still at the point of retrogradation <note>The "stationary" point before a planet appears to move backward.</note> is like a healthy man whose health is failing him, though a little of it remains.
6. A planet standing still at the point of direct motion <note>The "stationary" point before a planet resumes its normal forward movement.</note> is like a sick man who later recovers and sees the beginning of his health.
7. An <term>obsessed</term> <note>original: "obsessus"; in astrology, this refers to a planet "besieged" or trapped between two malefic planets.</note> planet is like one living in fear between two enemies; that is, when it is between two <term>ill-fortunes</term> <note>The "malefic" planets, typically Mars and Saturn, which were thought to bring challenges.</note>.
8. When a planet is between two <term>fortunes</term> <note>The "benefic" planets, typically Venus and Jupiter, which were thought to bring ease and success.</note>, it is like a man eating, drinking, and feeling secure.

97 When a malefic planet is in the ascendant, and a malefic is also in the second house, the question will fall away and proceed toward misfortune.

98 When the ascendant is diminished in <term>ascensions<note>original: "ascensionibus." Refers to the time it takes for a sign to rise; "short ascension" signs were sometimes viewed as less stable or swift-moving.</note></term>, and its lord is in a descending place in the sixth or ninth [house], the seeker will hope for things that they will not obtain; and when there is a benefic in the third from the ascendant, and a malefic in...

<summary>This page lists astrological rules for predicting the outcome of personal inquiries based on the positions of Jupiter and the malefic planets (Saturn and Mars) within specific "houses" of a zodiac chart. It emphasizes how a well-placed "benefic" planet like Jupiter can negate the negative influence of "malefic" planets.</summary>

...in the <term>ascendant<note>The zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of the question, representing the person asking (the seeker).</note></term>: the seeker will be of poor application to the business <note>original: "prauę applicationis ad negocium." 99 When a planet happens to be losing its time of ascension <note>original: "perdens de tempore ascensionis." This likely refers to a planet that is weakening or "falling" in its celestial strength based on its position in the zodiac.</note>, the seeker will encounter misfortune at the end of their business, even after its determination and achievement.

100 When a <term>malefic planet<note>original: "planeta infortuna." Traditionally Saturn or Mars, planets believed to bring challenges, delays, or hardship.</note></term> is received in the <term>angles<note>original: "angulis." These are the four most powerful houses in an astrological chart—the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th—where planets are most capable of producing significant real-world effects.</note></term>, it will grant and facilitate the seeker’s business; however, it will eventually take back what it gave. The knowledge of <term>reception<note>original: "scientia receptionis." An astrological condition where a planet resides in a sign ruled by another planet, creating a relationship of "hospitality" or mutual support.</note></term> occurs when a planet is in its own house or the house of its <term>exaltation<note>A specific sign where a planet's influence is considered exceptionally noble and powerful.</note></term>, safe from misfortune.

->THE END<-

<summary>This final page of the collection concludes a series of 100 astrological rules, warning that even successful outcomes can be undermined by "malefic" planets or waning celestial strength. It ends by defining "reception" and "exaltation," key concepts for determining if a planet has the dignity to produce a good result.</summary>
